expectations.text: Enhanced prompt is delivered in a clearly marked copy-paste block, separate from commentary
expectations.evidence: Under the heading '## Enhanced prompt', the full rewritten prompt is in a fenced code block, with commentary ('What changed and why', 'Optional additions') kept outside it.

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt states the intent/goal (raise conversion, Black Friday deadline), not just the task
expectations.evidence: Block opens with: 'The business goal: checkout conversion needs to go up before Black Friday, so the priority is removing anything that makes shoppers abandon or fail to complete a purchase — not a visual redesign.'

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt names the specific known bug (coupon field crashes on empty input)
expectations.evidence: Block says: 'Fix the known bug: the coupon code field crashes when submitted with empty input. Find the root cause, fix it...'

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt defines success criteria or scope boundaries (what 'better' means, what's out of scope)
expectations.evidence: Block includes both: 'Boundaries: don't redesign the layout, restructure components beyond what the fixes require, or add new features' and 'Done means: the coupon field handles empty, invalid, and valid input without crashing; every bug you fixed has a test or a manual repro step...'

expectations.text: Response includes change notes explaining what changed and why (not just the rewritten prompt)
expectations.evidence: Dedicated '## What changed and why' section with five bulleted rationales, e.g. 'Stated the intent (conversion before Black Friday, not aesthetics) — "make it better" would otherwise get resolved as a visual polish pass'.

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt does not name any specific AI model or vendor
expectations.evidence: The fenced enhanced-prompt block contains no model or vendor names (no Claude/GPT/Anthropic/OpenAI etc.); it refers only to the app, the bug, and generic 'the model/agent' framing outside the block.

claims.claim: The response inferred assumptions instead of asking clarifying questions, per the user's instruction
claims.evidence: Opens with 'Since you asked for a one-shot rewrite, here's what I inferred rather than asked' and lists the inferences explicitly.

claims.claim: Optional additions are conditioned on user context (test suite access, file locations, analytics)
claims.evidence: Each optional addition states its precondition, e.g. 'If the agent has access to your test suite / dev server, add: ...'

suggestions.reason: All six assertions pass for both the with_skill and without_skill runs, so this eval does not discriminate the skill's contribution. Consider assertions on the skill's distinctive behaviors, e.g. stating inferred assumptions up front, or offering conditional optional additions rather than baking speculation into the prompt.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are individually reasonable but collectively too easy for a strong baseline model; both runs score 6/6.
